   in the court's own words, and one provision nobody contested. One example
   carries only risk type 1, one only risk type 2, one both. Note how a single
   provision can carry more than one defect, and of more than one type. That is
   the standard to apply — not your own sense of what looks badly drafted.

   cannot be seen from one provision alone. It is long — read it in pieces, and
   use Grep to chase a defined term or a cross-reference wherever it leads.

   The court read them together with this one, and a provision here can fail to
   square with something in one of them — a policy against the endorsement that
   amends it, a memorandum against the declaration of trust that governs it.
   Skim what each one is, and go back to it when a provision points outward.
   You judge only the provisions in `provisions.json`, every one of which is
   from `contract.txt`; the context documents are there to be read, not judged.

For each provision return an **issue list** — one entry per distinct defect a
court could be asked to construe, each with its own probability. A provision may
carry several issues of one type, issues of both types, or nothing specific at
all.

Each issue is three fields:

  * `issue` — two sentences naming THIS defect. For type 1, the ambiguous
    term or the general-vs-specific tension. For type 2, the other provision it
    cannot be squared with, **named**. One issue, one defect: if you write "and
    also", that is a second issue.
  * `type` — `1` for an intrinsic textual defect visible in the provision
    itself, `2` for a defect in its relationship to the rest of the instrument.
  * `prob` — that a court would have something to construe on account of THIS
    issue, to two decimal places on a 0.01 grid (0.03, 0.17, 0.62 — do not round
    to the nearest 0.05). Always greater than 0: the entry exists because the
    defect does, and one you would put at 0 is one you should not have listed.

        "issues": [
          {"issue": "\"Reasonable efforts\" is not defined and the section

            "type": 1, "prob": 0.44}
        ]},
      {"clause_id": "c002", "issues": []},
      ...
    ]}

entry for "no issue here".

into a sentence but would not bet on is a real entry with a low probability:
0.08, 0.15, 0.20. It is not a reason to write nothing, and the low end of the
range is where most named issues belong. Uncertainty goes into the probability;
the empty list is only for a provision you can find nothing to name in. The
question that decides between them is not "am I confident?" but "can I say what
is wrong?" — a provision you scored 0.15 on ranks far above one you left empty.

**How long the list should normally be: empty, or exactly one entry.**

  * A provision you can find nothing to name in gets an empty list — not an
    entry saying so, nothing. Reach it by looking and finding nothing, not by
    deciding the defect you can see is too weak to write down.

    of whichever type it is, at whatever probability it deserves — 0.10 if that
    is what you think. The other type gets no entry at all.

    them only when the extra defect is obvious and you would put a genuinely
    high probability on it in its own right. If you are hedging about the second
    issue, it is not a second issue — leave it out and let the first issue's
    probability carry your uncertainty. The test: could you state the second
    defect to a judge, on its own, and expect to be taken seriously?

Rules for that file:

  * one judgment for EVERY id in `provisions.json`, all 159 of them, same order
    — including every provision you found nothing in, which gets `"issues": []`
  * an OMITTED provision is not the same as an empty list. A provision you leave
    out counts as unanswered, and you will be asked for it again; a provision
    with an empty list is judged and done. Never drop a provision to say it is
    clean — write the empty list
  * `clause_id` copied exactly — `c001`, not the provision's heading
  * a type with no entry is read as probability 0, and that is what it means —
    do not add an entry for the other type just to keep the two balanced
  * keep each `issue` to two sentences; you are producing a judgment, not a
    memorandum
  * a long issue list is not a better answer; it is usually a wrong one
  * write the file even if you are unsure about some provisions; a provision
    missing from the file is scored as "not risky" at probability 0 anyway, so
    leaving it out buys you nothing and loses the judgment you did make

**Work in batches and flush as you go.** Do not hold 159 judgments in your head
and write them all at the end: if the session ends early, everything unwritten
is lost and scored against you. Instead judge fifty or so provisions, write them
out, then continue with the next batch. Write each batch to its OWN numbered
file — `predictions_001.json`, `predictions_002.json`, and so on, each with the
same `judgments` shape. They are read together and concatenated, so never
rewrite an earlier file and never repeat an id.

When every provision in `provisions.json` has been written to one of those
files, stop. Reply with one line: how many judgments you wrote.

MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT /
Between

THE NEW YORK TIMES COMPANY

and
NEWSPAPER AND MAIL BDELIVERERS!' UNION

OF NEW YORK AND VICINITY

This Memorandum of Agreement made and entered into by and
between The New York Times Company ("The Times") and the
Newspaper and Mail Deliverers' Union of New York and Vicinity
("union") shall extend the current Collective Bargaining
Agreement, which expires on March 30, 1993, until March 30, 2000
to the extent such Collective Bargaining Agreement is not

modified by, or inconsistent with, the terms and conditions set

forth herein.

Sewr Sd

furSuan
Agreement, the parties have negotiated in good faith in order to
resolve issues arising from technological innovations and new

methods of operation to be instituted at Edison.

The parties restate their commitment to the orderly,

successful and efficient start-up and operations at

Ts\FSS\WP5S 1\FIRM\OS87\50000. FSS 55553-0462 #T21P (386) 05/16/92 5: tépm

FUNDO0001098


Edison. The parties further restate their commitment to
negotiate those issues arising out of the start-up and
operations at any other new or rebuilt facilities operated
by The Times in the territorial jurisdiction of the NMDU.
In furtherance of these commitments, the parties agree as

follows:

A. Except as otherwise provided herein, the contract |
as modified by this Memorandum shall have full
force and effect at any new or rebuilt facility
operated by The Times within the territorial

jurisdiction of the NMDU.

B. The parties agree that the technological
innovations, methods of operation, scheduling
practices and/or working conditions to be employed
at Edison, e.g. palletization, tractor-trailer
delivery to wholesalers, and card reader system,
may also be employed at any new or rebuilt

facility to be operated -y The Times.

c. The parties acknowledge that The Times may, at a
new or rebuilt facility, seek to employ further
technological innovations, methods of operation,

scheduling practices, and/or working conditions

FUNDO0001099


different from and/or in addition to those
employed at Edison. In that event, and in the
event that after a period of 120 days, the parties
are unable through negotiation to resolve any
disputes over such matters, the parties agree to
submit the disputes to final and binding interest

arbitration before the Merits Arbitrator.

2. The Contract Arbitrator

Either party may, within the sixty (60) day period
preceding March 30 of each contract year,

terminate the incumbent "Merits Arbitrator", with

the termination to become effective upon the

selection by the parties, pursuant to the
procedure set forth below, of a new "Merits
Arbitrator". The Merits Arbitrator shall, except _
as otherwise provided herein, be responsible for
hearing and resolving all grievances, differences
and disputes initiated after his selection that
arise out of the interpretation or application of
the Agreement at all facilities operated by. The
Times within the territorial jurisdiction of the

NMDU.

FUNDO0001100


In the event that either party exercises its right
as described above to terminate the Merits
Arbitrator, and in the event that the parties fail
to reach agreement on a new Merits Arbitrator, the
Merits Arbitrator shall be selected pursuant to
the Voluntary Labor Arbitration Rules of the

American Arbitration Association.

Either party may, within the sixty (60) day period
preceding September 30 of each contract year,
terminate the incumbent Status Quo Arbitrator.
Said termination shall become effective upon the
selection by the parties of a new Status Quo
Arbitrator pursuant to the procedure described in

paragraph B above.

3. Buyouts

A.

In order to effectuate necessary manning
reductions at Edison in the nost fair and.
equitable manner, The Times will offer a voluntary
buyout to all active NMDU RSHs employed by the
Times, including foremen, and to all active
"Eligible Group I Employees," as defined below.
The buyout offer will be in accordance with the

terms and conditions as set forth in Attachments A

4

FUNDOO001101


and B attached hereto and made part hereof. The

following summarizes the elements of the offer:

1)

2)

3)

The amount of $70,000 will be offered to all
active NMDU RSHs in the form of lump sum
payments or annuities.

The amount of $35,000 will be offered to all
active "Eligible Group I Employees" in the
form of lump sum payments or annuities. For
purposes of this Agreement, "Eligible Group I
Employees" shall mean individuals included on
the Times Group I list as of the date of
signing of this Agreement who are still on

the Group I list on the date of ratification.

For the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and
1995, The Times will make health and welfare
contributions to the NMDU Health and Welfare
Fund for a minimum of 450 Full Time
Equivalents. For purposes of this Agreement,
260 shifts per year shall constitute one Full
Time Equivalent. The contributions shall be
based on the highest straight time scale
applicable for the contract year in which the

contributions are made. It is understood

5

FUNDO001 102


5)

that these contributions shall be in lieu of
and not in addition to those that would

otherwise be called for by the Agreement.

Upon termination of the buyout offer, and
upon severance from the payroll of those
accepting the buyout, The Times will make a
one-time contribution to the NMDU Health and
Welfare Fund which will be equal to fifteen
thousand dollars ($15,000) multiplied by the
number of active NMDU RSHs who take the
buyout. In addition, The Times will make a
one-time contribution to the NMDU Health and
Welfare Fund which will be equal to seven
thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500)
multiplied by the number of active Eligible

Group I Employees who take the buyout.

The Times will make pension contributions to
the NMDU Pension Fund on behalf of RSHs who
accept the buyout, to age 65 or for a period
of five (5) years, whichever comes first.
The contributions shall be based on the
highest straight time scale applicable for
the contract year in which the contributions

are made.

FUNDO0001103


6) The Times life insurance will be continued on
behalf of RSHs that accept the buyout, to age

65 or for 5 years, whichever comes first.

7) The buyout offer will remain open for a

period of 45 days commencing promptly after

ratification of this Agreement.

4. RSH Procedures Subsequent to Buyout

Ae

Upon termination of the buyout offer, and upon
severance from the payroll of those accepting the
buyout, The Times will add to the RSH list the
number of employees necessary to reach 370 regular
situations. Such additions to the list shall come
from the Eligible Group I Employees who do not

accept the buyout.

tligible Group I Employees who do not become RSHs
as a result of the procedure described in
paragraph A shall, during the term of this
Agreement, and up to a maximum of 370, replace, on
a one-for-one basis, RSHs who cease to be
employees of the Times for any reason, e.g.,
death, retirement, resignation, discharge, etc.

This replacement procedure shall apply only to

FUNDO001 104


Eligible Group I Employees as defined above.
Eligible Group I Employees who become RSHs as a

er result of this replacement procedure shall have a

length of contract employment guarantee governed
by the terms of Appendix A. Once the replacement
procedure has been completed, there shall be no
[oo less than 270 RSHS during the term of this

Agreement.

Cc. Once the procedure described in paragraph A is
completed, The Times will not be required to
replace on a daily, nightly, or weekly basis RSHs
who are scheduled to work at any facility, but are
absent for any reason, e.g. illness, vacation,
jury duty, personal day, etc., unless the total

number of RSHs who report to work is insufficient

to satisfy specific manning requirements.

D. In the ‘ever.c that a regular situation is vacated
after the procedure described in paragraph A is
completed, either because a RSH ceases to be an
employee of The Times for any reason, e.g., death,
retirement, resignation, discharge, etc., or

: because the RSH bids off the job: (i) an employee

| need not be promoted to the status of RSH unless

necessary to comply either with the replacement

FUNDO001105


precedure set forth in paragraph B above or with
specific manning requirements; and (ii) following
discussion with the Union, the vacated situation
may be filled or eliminated at the discretion of
The Times, unless the situation must be filled to
comply with specific manning requirements. As
attrition below 370 RSHs occurs, The Times shall
also have the right to consolidate segments of
vacated situations into corresponding "open"
segments of the existing bid work schedules of
other RSH’s, provided that the RSH’s with the
corresponding "open'! segments will be permitted to
bid by seniority on the segments to be
consolidated. In the event there are no bidders,
the segments will be assigned to the junior of
such RSH’s. It is further provided that The Times
may not so consolidate vacated situations in which
one run constitutes the entire day’s or night’s
work for a shift on three or more shifts each

week.

5. West Side Direct Reorganization

Immediately following the closure of the forty-five
(45) day buyout offer peried, the Times shall have the

right to consolidate and otherwise reorganize all

9

FUNDO0001106


existing daily West Side Direct routes, including both
daily and Sunday routes. A reduction of fifty percent
‘ee (50%) of the existing daily West Side Direct routes
: will be permitted in this reorganization. As a result

of that reduction, there will be thirteen (13) daily

West Side Direct routes, and thirteen (13) chauffeur
and sixteen (16) tailmen assignments will remain. With
respect to the Sunday West Side Direct routes, there
will be twelve (12) routes carrying Sunday Main and
Sports. As a result of this reduction, twelve (12)

chauffeurs and twelve (12) tailmen will remain.
6. Bulldog Reorganization

a~ Immediately following the closure of the forty-five

(45) day buyout offer period, The Times shall have the

right to consolidate and otherwise reorganize all
existing Saturday Night Bulldeg (SNBD) routes. The
routes may deliver the four-she c (Package 3 when

Edison opens) and the Sunday Main and Sports together.

The reorganization shall be subject only to the
limitation that the minimum number of all SNBD routes
on Saturday evening shall be forty (40). Relay cars

and flash cars will be used based on the needs of the

10

FUNDO001107


operation, provided that there shall be a minimum of
two (2) flash cars. As a result of the reduction in
SNBD routes, forty (40) chauffeur and forty-eight (48)
